Yehu assembled all the people and said to them, “Achav served Ba'al little; Yehu shall serve him much!

Therefore, summon to me all the prophets of Ba'al, all his worshipers, and all his priests: let no one fail to come, for I am going to hold a great sacrifice for Ba'al. Whoever fails to come shall forfeit his life.” Yehu was acting with guile in order to exterminate the worshipers of Ba'al.
Yehu gave orders to convoke a solemn assembly for Ba'al, and one was proclaimed.
Yehu sent word throughout Yisrael, and all the worshipers of Ba'al came, not a single one remained behind. They came into the temple of Ba'al, and the temple of Ba'al was filled from end to end.
He said to the man in charge of the wardrobe,dMeaning of Heb. uncertain. “Bring out the vestments for all the worshipers of Ba'al”; and he brought vestments out for them.

Then Yehu and Yehonadav son of Rechav came into the temple of Ba'al, and they said to the worshipers of Ba'al, “Search and make sure that there are no worshipers of Hashem among you, but only worshipers of Ba'al.”

So they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. But Yehu had stationed eighty of his men outside and had said, “Whoever permits the escape of a single one of the men I commit to your charge shall forfeit life for life.”

When Yehu had finished presenting the burnt offering, he said to the guards and to the officers, “Come in and strike them down; let no man get away!” The guards and the officers struck them down with the sword and left them lying where they were; then they proceeded to the interioreLit. “city.” of the temple of Ba'al.
They brought out the pillarsfEmendation yields “sacred posts”; cf. Devarim 12.3. of the temple of Ba'al and burned them.
They destroyed the pillargEmendation yields “altar.” of Ba'al, and they tore down the temple of Ba'al and turned it into latrines, as is still the case.
Thus Yehu eradicated the Ba'al from Yisrael.
However, Yehu did not turn away from the sinful objects by which Yerovam son of Nevat had caused Yisrael to sin, namely, the golden calves at Beit El and at Dan.

Hashem said to Yehu, “Because you have acted well and done what was pleasing to Me, having carried out all that I desired upon the House of Achav, four generations of your descendants shall occupy the throne of Yisrael.”
But Yehu was not careful to follow the Teaching of Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael, with all his heart; he did not turn away from the sins that Yerovam had caused Yisrael to commit.
In those days Hashem began to reduce Yisrael; and Chazael harassed them throughout the territory of Yisrael
east of the Yarden, all the land of Gilad—the Gadi, the Reuveni, and the Menashi—from Aroer, by the Wadi Arnon, up to Gilad and Bashan.
The other events of Yehu’s reign, and all his actions, and all his exploits, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yisrael.
Yehu slept with his fathers and he was buried in Shomron; he was succeeded as king by his son Yehoachaz.
Yehu reigned over Yisrael for twenty-eight years in Shomron.
When Atalyahu, the mother of Achazyahu, learned that her son was dead, she promptly killed off all who were of royal stock.

But Yehosheva, daughter of King Yoram and sister of Achazyahu, secretly took Achazyahu’s son Yoash away from among the princes who were being slain, and [put]aCf. Divrei Hayamim II 22.11. him and his nurse in a bedroom. And theybDivrei Hayamim II 22.11 reads “she.” kept him hidden from Atalyahu so that he was not put to death.
He stayed with her for six years, hidden in the House of Hashem,cYehosheva was the wife of the high priest Yehoyada; cf. Divrei Hayamim II 22.11. while Atalyahu reigned over the land.

In the seventh year, Yehoyada sent for the chiefs of the hundreds of the KaridPerhaps the Kreti (cf. Shmuel II 20.23) or the Carians. They were members of the king’s bodyguard. and of the guards, and had them come to him in the House of Hashem. He made a pact with them, exacting an oath from them in the House of Hashem, and he showed them the king’s son.
He instructed them: “This is what you must do: One-third of those who are on duty for the week eHeb. “and who keep guard.”shall maintain guard-e over the royal palace;

another third shall be [stationed] at the fDivrei Hayamim II 23.5 reads “Foundation Gate.”Sur Gate;-f and the other third shall be at the gate behind gMeaning of Heb. uncertain.the guards; you shall keep guard over the House on every side.-g
The two divisions of yours who are off duty this week shall keep guard over the House of Hashem for the protection of the king.
You shall surround the king on every side, every man with his weapons at the ready; and whoever breaks through the ranks shall be killed. Stay close to the king in his comings and goings.”
The chiefs of hundreds did just as Yehoyada ordered: Each took his men—those who were on duty that week and those who were off duty that week—and they presented themselves to Yehoyada the priest.
The priest gave the chiefs of hundreds King David’s spearshDivrei Hayamim II 23.9 adds “and shields.” and quivers that were kept in the House of Hashem.
The guards, each with his weapons at the ready, stationed themselves—from the south end of the House to the north end of the House, at the altar and the House—to guard the king on every side.

[Yehoyada] then brought out the king’s son, and placed upon him the crown and the insignia.gMeaning of Heb. uncertain. They anointed him and proclaimed him king; they clapped their hands and shouted, “Long live the king!”
When Atalyahu heard the shouting of the guards [and] the people, she came out to the people in the House of Hashem.

She looked about and saw the king standing by the pillar, as was the custom, the chiefs with their trumpets beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Atalyahu rent her garments and cried out, “Treason, treason!”

Then the priest Yehoyada gave the command to the army officers, the chiefs of hundreds, and said to them, “Take her out gMeaning of Heb. uncertain.between the ranks-g and, if anyone follows her, put him to the sword.” For the priest thought: “Let her not be put to death in the House of Hashem.”
They cleared a passageway for her and she entered the royal palace through the horses’ entrance: there she was put to death.
And Yehoyada solemnized the covenant between Hashem, on the one hand, and the king and the people, on the other—as well as between the king and the people—that they should be the people of Hashem.

Thereupon all the people of the land went to the temple of Ba'al. They tore it down and smashed its altars and images to bits, and they slew Matan, the priest of Ba'al, in front of the altars. [Yehoyada] the priest then placed guards over the House of Hashem.

He took the chiefs of hundreds, the Kari,dPerhaps the Kreti (cf. Shmuel II 20.23) or the Carians. They were members of the king’s bodyguard. the guards, and all the people of the land, and they escorted the king from the House of Hashem into the royal palace by the gate of the guards. And he ascended the royal throne.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. As for Atalyahu, she had been put to the sword in the royal palace.
Yehoash was seven years old when he became king.
Yehoash began his reign in the seventh year of Yehu, and he reigned in Yerushalayim forty years. His mother’s name was Tzivyah of Beer Sheva.
All his days Yehoash did what was pleasing to Hashem, as the priest Yehoyada instructed him.
The shrines, however, were not removed; the people continued to sacrifice and offer at the shrines.

Yehoash said to the priests, “All the money, current money, brought into the House of Hashem as sacred donations—aSee Vayikra 27.2–8.any money a man may pay as the money equivalent of persons,-a or any other money that a man may be minded to bring to the House of Hashem—
let the priests receive it, each from his benefactor; they, in turn, shall make repairs on the House, wherever damage may be found.”
But in the twenty-third year of King Yehoash, [it was found that] the priests had not made the repairs on the House.

So King Yehoash summoned the priest Yehoyada and the other priests and said to them, “Why have you not kept the House in repair? Now do not accept money from your benefactors any more, but have it donated for the repair of the House.”
The priests agreed that they would neither accept money from the people nor make repairs on the House.

And the priest Yehoyada took a chest and bored a hole in its lid. He placed it at the right side of the altar as one entered the House of Hashem, and the priestly guards of the threshold deposited there all the money that was brought into the House of Hashem.
Whenever they saw that there was much money in the chest, the royal scribe and the high priest would come up and put the money accumulated in the House of Hashem into bags, and they would count it.

Then they would deliver the money bMeaning of Heb. uncertain.that was weighed out-b to the overseers of the work, who were in charge of the House of Hashem. These, in turn, used to pay the carpenters and the laborers who worked on the House of Hashem,

and the masons and the stonecutters. They also paid for wood and for quarried stone with which to make the repairs on the House of Hashem, and for every other expenditure that had to be made in repairing the House.
However, no silver bowls and no snuffers, basins, or trumpets—no vessels of gold or silver—were made at the House of Hashem from the money brought into the House of Hashem;
this was given only to the overseers of the work for the repair of the House of Hashem.
No check was kept on the men to whom the money was delivered to pay the workers; for they dealt honestly.
Money brought cSee Vayikra 5.15.as a guilt offering or as a sin offering-c was not deposited in the House of Hashem; it went to the priests.
At that time, King Chazael of Aram came up and attacked Gat and captured it; and Chazael proceeded to march on Yerushalayim.

Thereupon King Yoash of Yehudah took all the objects that had been consecrated by his fathers, Kings Yehoshafat, Yehoram, and Achazyahu of Yehudah, and by himself, and all the gold that there was in the treasuries of the Temple of Hashem and in the royal palace, and he sent them to King Chazael of Aram, who then turned back from his march on Yerushalayim.
The other events of Yoash’s reign, and all his actions, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yehudah.
His courtiers formed a conspiracy against Yoash and assassinated him at Beit Milo bMeaning of Heb. uncertain.that leads down to Sila.-b
The courtiers who assassinated him were Yozachar son of Shimat and Yehozavad son of Shomer. He died and was buried with his fathers in the City of David; and his son Amatzyahu succeeded him as king.
In the twenty-third year of King Yoash son of Achazyahu of Yehudah, Yehoachaz son of Yehu became king over Yisrael in Shomron—for seventeen years.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem. He persisted in the sins which Yerovam son of Nevat had caused Yisrael to commit; he did not depart from them.
Hashem was angry with Yisrael and He repeatedly delivered them into the hands of King Chazael of Aram and into the hands of Ben Hadad son of Chazael.
But Yehoachaz pleaded with Hashem; and Hashem listened to him, for He saw the suffering that the king of Aram inflicted upon Yisrael.
So Hashem granted Yisrael a deliverer, and they gained their freedom from Aram; and Yisrael dwelt in its homes as before.
However, they did not depart from the sins which the House of Yerovam had caused Yisrael to commit; they persisted in them. Even the sacred post stood in Shomron.

aThis verse would read well after v. 3.In fact, Yehoachaz was left with a force of only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers; for the king of Aram had decimated them and trampled them like the dust under his feet.
The other events of Yehoachaz’s reign, and all his actions and his exploits, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yisrael.
Yehoachaz slept with his fathers and he was buried in Shomron; his son Yoash succeeded him as king.
In the thirty-seventh year of King Yoash of Yehudah, Yehoash son of Yehoachaz became king of Yisrael in Shomron—for sixteen years.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem; he did not depart from any of the sins which Yerovam son of Nevat had caused Yisrael to commit; he persisted in them.
The other events of Yoash’s reign, and all his actions, and his exploits in his war with King Amatzyahu of Yehudah, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yisrael.
Yoash slept with his fathers and Yerovam occupied his throne; Yoash was buried in Shomron with the kings of Yisrael.

Elisha had been stricken with the illness of which he was to die, and King Yoash of Yisrael went down to see him. He wept over him and cried, “Father, father! bOn Elisha as defender of Yisrael, see chapters 6–8.Yisrael’s chariots and horsemen!”-b
Elisha said to him, “Get a bow and arrows”; and he brought him a bow and arrows.
Then he said to the king of Yisrael, “Grasp the bow!” And when he had grasped it, Elisha put his hands over the king’s hands.

“Open the window toward the east,” he said; and he opened it. Elisha said, “Shoot!” and he shot. Then he said, “An arrow of victory for Hashem! An arrow of victory over Aram! You shall rout Aram completely at Afek.”
He said, “Now pick up the arrows.” And he picked them up. “Strike the ground!” he said to the king of Yisrael; and he struck three times and stopped.

The man of Elokim was angry with him and said to him, cLit. “to strike.”“If only you had struck-c five or six times! Then you would have annihilated Aram; as it is, you shall defeat Aram only three times.”
Elisha died and he was buried. Now bands of Moavim used to invade the land dMeaning of Heb. uncertain; emendation yields “year by year.”at the coming of every year.-d

Once a man was being buried, when the people caught sight of such a band; so they threw the corpseeHeb. “the man.” into Elisha’s grave and fHeb. “he made off.”made off.-f When the [dead] man came in contact with Elisha’s bones, he came to life and stood up.
King Chazael of Aram had oppressed Bnei Yisrael throughout the reign of Yehoachaz.

But Hashem was gracious and merciful to them, and He turned back to them for the sake of His covenant with Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov. He refrained from destroying them, and He still did not cast them out from His presence.
When King Chazael of Aram died, his son Ben Hadad succeeded him as king;

and then Yehoash son of Yehoachaz recovered from Ben Hadad son of Chazael the towns which had been taken from his father Yehoachaz in war. Three times Yoash defeated him, and he recovered the towns of Yisrael.
In the second year of King Yoash son of Yoachaz of Yisrael, Amatzyahu son of King Yoash of Yehudah became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim; his mother’s name was Yehoadan of Yerushalayim.
He did what was pleasing to Hashem, but not like his ancestor David; he did just as his father Yoash had done.
However, the shrines were not removed; the people continued to sacrifice and make offerings at the shrines.
Once he had the kingdom firmly in his grasp, he put to death the courtiers who had assassinated his father the king.

But he did not put to death the children of the assassins, in accordance with what is written in the Book of the Teaching of Moshe, where Hashem commanded, “Parents shall not be put to death for children, nor children be put to death for parents; a person shall be put to death only for his own crime.”aDevarim 24.16.
He defeated ten thousand Edomim in the Valley of Salt, and he captured Sela in battle and renamed it Yokte'el, as is still the case.
Then Amatzyahu sent envoys to King Yehoash son of Yehoachaz son of Yehu of Yisrael, with this message: “Come, let us confrontbI.e., in battle. each other.”

King Yehoash of Yisrael sent back this message to King Amatzyahu of Yehudah: “The thistle in Levanon sent this message to the cedar in Levanon, ‘Give your daughter to my son in marriage.’ But a wild beast in Levanon went by and trampled down the thistle.
Because you have defeated Edom, you have become arrogant. Stay home and enjoy your glory, rather than provoke disaster and fall, dragging Yehudah down with you.”
But Amatzyahu paid no heed; so King Yehoash of Yisrael advanced, and he and King Amatzyahu of Yehudah confronted each other at Beit Shemesh in Yehudah.
The Yehudim were routed by Yisrael, and they all fled to their homes.

King Yehoash of Yisrael captured King Amatzyahu son of Yehoash son of Achazyahu of Yehudah at Beit Shemesh. He marched on Yerushalayim, and he made a breach of four hundred cubits in the wall of Yerushalayim, fromcHeb. “at.” the Efraim Gate to the Corner Gate.
He carried off all the gold and silver and all the vessels that there were in the House of Hashem and in the treasuries of the royal palace, as well as hostages; and he returned to Shomron.
The other events of Yehoash’s reign, and all his actions and exploits, and his war with King Amatzyahu of Yehudah, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yisrael.
Yehoash slept with his fathers, and was buried in Shomron with the kings of Yisrael; his son Yerovam succeeded him as king.
King Amatzyahu son of Yoash of Yehudah lived fifteen years after the death of King Yehoash son of Yehoachaz of Yisrael.
The other events of Amatzyahu’s reign are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yehudah.
A conspiracy was formed against him in Yerushalayim and he fled to Lachish; but they sent men after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.
They brought back his body on horses, and he was buried with his fathers in Yerushalayim, in the City of David.
Then all the people of Yehudah took Azaryah, who was sixteen years old, and proclaimed him king to succeed his father Amatzyahu.
It was he who rebuilt Eilat and restored it to Yehudah, after King [Amatzyahu] slept with his fathers.
In the fifteenth year of King Amatzyahu son of Yoash of Yehudah, King Yerovam son of Yoash of Yisrael became king in Shomron—for forty-one years.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem; he did not depart from all the sins that Yerovam son of Nevat had caused Yisrael to commit.

It was he who restored the territory of Yisrael from Levo Chamat to the sea of the Arabah, in accordance with the promise that Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael, had made through His servant, the prophet Yonah son of Amitai from Gat Hachefer.
For Hashem saw the very bitter plight of Yisrael, with neither dSee note at Melachim I 14.10.bond nor free-d left, and with none to help Yisrael.
And Hashem resolved not to blot out the name of Yisrael from under heaven; and he delivered them through Yerovam son of Yoash.

The other events of Yerovam’s reign, and all his actions and exploits, how he fought and recovered Damesek and Chamat eEmendation yields “for Yisrael.”for Yehudah in Yisrael,-e are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yisrael.
Yerovam slept with his fathers, the kings of Yisrael, and his son Zecharyah succeeded him as king.
In the twenty-seventh year of King Yerovam of Yisrael, Azaryah son of King Amatzyahu of Yehudah became king.
He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Yerushalayim; his mother’s name was Yecholyah of Yerushalayim.
He did what was pleasing to Hashem, just as his father Amatzyahu had done.
However, the shrines were not removed; the people continued to sacrifice and make offerings at the shrines.

Hashem struck the king with a plague, and he was a leper until the day of his death; he lived aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.in isolated quarters,-a while Yotam, the king’s son, was in charge of the palace and governed the people of the land.
The other events of Azaryah’s reign, and all his actions, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yehudah.
Azaryah slept with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the City of David; his son Yotam succeeded him as king.
In the thirty-eighth year of King Azaryah of Yehudah, Zecharyah son of Yerovam became king over Yisrael in Shomron—for six months.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem, as his fathers had done; he did not depart from the sins which Yerovam son of Nevat had caused Yisrael to commit.
Shalum son of Yavesh conspired against him and struck him down bSome Septuagint mss. read “at Yivleam.”before the people-b and killed him, and succeeded him as king.
The other events of Zecharyah’s reign are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yisrael.
This was in accord with the word that Hashem had spoken to Yehu: “Four generations of your descendants shall occupy the throne of Yisrael.” And so it came about.cCf. 10.30.
Shalum son of Yavesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of King Uziyahu of Yehudah, and he reigned in Shomron one month.
Then Menachem son of Gadi set out from Tirtzah and came to Shomron; he attacked Shalum son of Yavesh in Shomron and killed him, and he succeeded him as king.
The other events of Shalum’s reign, and the conspiracy that he formed, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yisrael.

At that time, aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.[marching] from Tirtzah,-a Menachem subdued Tifsach and all who were in it, and its territory; and because it did not surrender, he massacred [its people] and ripped open all its pregnant women.
In the thirty-ninth year of King Azaryah of Yehudah, Menachem son of Gadi became king over Yisrael in Shomron—for ten years.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem; throughout his days he did not depart from the sins which Yerovam son of Nevat had caused Yisrael to commit.
King Pul of Ashur invaded the land, and Menachem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver that he might support him and strengthen his hold on the kingdom.
Menachem exacted the money from Yisrael: every man of means had to pay fifty shekels of silver for the king of Ashur. The king of Ashur withdrew and did not remain in the land.
The other events of Menachem’s reign, and all his actions, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yisrael.
Menachem slept with his fathers, and his son Pekachyah succeeded him as king.
In the fiftieth year of King Azaryah of Yehudah, Pekachyah son of Menachem became king over Yisrael in Shomron—for two years.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem; he did not depart from the sins which Yerovam son of Nevat had caused Yisrael to commit.

His aide, Pekach son of Remalyahu, conspired against him and struck him down in the royal palace in Shomron; with him were fifty Giladi, aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.with men from Argov and Arye;-a and he killed him and succeeded him as king.
The other events of Pekachyah’s reign, and all his actions, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yisrael.
In the fifty-second year of King Azaryah of Yehudah, Pekach son of Remalyahu became king over Yisrael and Shomron—for twenty years.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem; he did not depart from the sins which Yerovam son of Nevat had caused Yisrael to commit.

In the days of King Pekach of Yisrael, King Tiglat Pileser of Ashur came and captured Iyon, Abel- beth-maacah, Yanochah, Kedesh, Chatzor—Gilad, Galil, the entire region of Naftali; and he deported dHeb. “them.”the inhabitants-d to Ashur.
Hoshea son of Elah conspired against Pekach son of Remalyahu, attacked him, and killed him. He succeeded him as king in the twentieth year of Yotam son of Uziyahu.
The other events of Pekach’s reign, and all his actions, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yisrael.
In the second year of King Pekach son of Remalyahu of Yisrael, Yotam son of King Uziyahu of Yehudah became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim; his mother’s name was Yerusha daughter of Tzadok.
He did what was pleasing to Hashem, just as his father Uziyahu had done.
However, the shrines were not removed; the people continued to sacrifice and make offerings at the shrines. It was he who built the Upper Gate of the House of Hashem.
The other events of Yotam’s reign, and all his actions, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yehudah.
In those days, Hashem began to incite King Retzin of Aram and Pekach son of Remalyahu against Yehudah.
Yotam slept with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of his ancestor David; his son Achaz succeeded him as king.
In the seventeenth year of Pekach son of Remalyahu, Achaz son of King Yotam of Yehudah became king.
Achaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. He did not do what was pleasing to Hashem his Elokim, as his ancestor David had done,
but followed the ways of the kings of Yisrael. He even consigned his son to the fire, in the abhorrent fashion of the nations which Hashem had dispossessed before Bnei Yisrael.
He sacrificed and made offerings at the shrines, on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
Then King Retzin of Aram and King Pekach son of Remalyahu of Yisrael advanced on Yerushalayim for battle. They besieged Achaz, but could not overcome [him].
At that time King Retzin of Aram recovered Eilat for Aram;aEmendation yields “Edom.” he drove out the Yehudim from Eilat, and Edomim came to Eilat and settled there, as is still the case.

Achaz sent messengers to King Tiglat Pileser of Ashur to say, “I am your servant and your son; come and deliver me from the hands of the king of Aram and from the hands of the king of Yisrael, who are attacking me.”
Achaz took the gold and silver that were on hand in the House of Hashem and in the treasuries of the royal palace and sent them as a gift to the king of Ashur.
The king of Ashur responded to his request; the king of Ashur marched against Damesek and captured it. He deported bHeb. “it.”its inhabitants-b to Kir and put Retzin to death.
When King Achaz went to Damesek to greet King Tiglat Pileser of Ashur, he saw the altar in Damesek. King Achaz sent the priest Uriyah a sketch of the altar and a detailed plan of its construction.
The priest Uriyah did just as King Achaz had instructed him from Damesek; the priest Uriyah built the altar before King Achaz returned from Damesek.
When the king returned from Damesek, and when the king saw the altar, the king drew near the altar, ascended it,
and offered his burnt offering and meal offering; he poured his libation, and he dashed the blood of his offering of well-being against the altar.

As for the bronze altar which had been before Hashem, he moved it from its place in front of the Temple, cMeaning of Heb. uncertain.between the [new] altar and the House of Hashem,-c and placed it on the north side of the [new] altar.

And King Achaz commanded the priest Uriyah: “On the greatdI.e., the new one. altar you shall offer the morning burnt offering and the evening meal offering and the king’s burnt offering and his meal offering, with the burnt offerings of all the people of the land, their meal offerings and their libations. And against it you shall dash the blood of all the burnt offerings and all the blood of the sacrifices. And I will decidecMeaning of Heb. uncertain. about the bronze altar.”eI.e., the old one, cf. v. 14.
Uriyah did just as King Achaz commanded.
King Achaz cut off the insets—the laver stands—and removed the lavers from them. He also removed the tank from the bronze oxen that supported it and set it on a stone pavement—

on account of the king of Ashur.fI.e., because of the metal given him in tribute. He also extended to the House of Hashem cMeaning of Heb. uncertain.the sabbath passage that had been built in the palace and the king’s outer entrance.-c
The other events of Achaz’s reign, and his actions, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yehudah.
Achaz slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David; his son Chizkiyahu succeeded him as king.
In the twelfth year of King Achaz of Yehudah, Hoshea son of Elah became king over Yisrael in Shomron—for nine years.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem, though not as much as the kings of Yisrael who preceded him.
King Shalmaneser marched against him, and Hoshea became his vassal and paid him tribute.

But the king of Ashur caught Hoshea in an act of treachery: he had sent envoys to King So of Mitzrayim, and he had not paid the tribute to the king of Ashur, as in previous years. And the king of Ashur arrested him and put him in prison.
Then the king of Ashur marched against the whole land; he came to Shomron and besieged it for three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Ashur captured Shomron. He deported Bnei Yisrael to Ashur and settled them in Chlach, at the [River] Chavor, at the River Gozan, and in the towns of Madai.
This happened because Bnei Yisrael sinned against Hashem their Elokim, who had freed them from the land of Mitzrayim, from the hand of Paroh king of Mitzrayim. They worshiped other gods
and followed the customs of the nations which Hashem had dispossessed before Bnei Yisrael and the customs which the kings of Yisrael had practiced.

Bnei Yisrael committedaMeaning of Heb. uncertain. against Hashem their Elokim acts which were not right: They built for themselves shrines in all their settlements, from watchtowers to fortified cities;
they set up pillars and sacred posts for themselves on every lofty hill and under every leafy tree;
and they offered sacrifices there, at all the shrines, like the nations whom Hashem had driven into exile before them. They committed wicked acts to vex Hashem,
and they worshiped fetishes concerning which Hashem had said to them, “You must not do this thing.”

Hashem warned Yisrael and Yehudah by every prophet [and] every seer, saying: “Turn back from your wicked ways, and observe My commandments and My laws, according to all the Teaching that I commanded your fathers and that I transmitted to you through My servants the prophets.”
But they did not obey; they stiffened their necks, like their fathers who did not have faith in Hashem their Elokim;

they spurned His laws and the covenant that He had made with their fathers, and the warnings He had given them. They went after delusion and were deluded; [they imitated] the nations that were about them, which Hashem had forbidden them to emulate.

They rejected all the commandments of Hashem their Elokim; they made molten idols for themselves—two calves—and they made a sacred post and they bowed down to all the host of heaven, and they worshiped Ba'al.
They consigned their sons and daughters to the fire; they practiced augury and divination, and gave themselves over to what was displeasing to Hashem and vexed Him.
Hashem was incensed at Yisrael and He banished them from His presence; none was left but the tribe of Yehudah alone.
Nor did Yehudah keep the commandments of Hashem their Elokim; they followed the customs that Yisrael had practiced.
So Hashem spurned all the offspring of Yisrael, and He afflicted them and delivered them into the hands of plunderers, and finally He cast them out from His presence.
For Yisrael broke away from the House of David, and they made Yerovam son of Nevat king. Yerovam caused Yisrael to stray from Hashem and to commit great sin,
and Bnei Yisrael persisted in all the sins which Yerovam had committed; they did not depart from them.
In the end, Hashem removed Yisrael from His presence, as He had warned them through all His servants the prophets. So Bnei Yisrael were deported from their land to Ashur, as is still the case.

The king of Ashur brought [people] from Bavel, Kutah, Avva, Chamat, and Sfarvayim, and he settled them in the towns of Shomron in place of Bnei Yisrael; they took possession of Shomron and dwelt in its towns.
When they first settled there, they did not worship Hashem; so Hashem sent lions against them which killed some of them.

They said to the king of Ashur: “The nations which you deported and resettled in the towns of Shomron do not know the rules of the Elokim of the land; therefore He has let lions loose against them which are killing them—for they do not know the rules of the Elokim of the land.”
The king of Ashur gave an order: “Send there one of the priests whom you have deported; let himbHeb. “them.” go and dwell there, and let him teach them the practices of the Elokim of the land.”
So one of the priests whom they had exiled from Shomron came and settled in Beit El; he taught them how to worship Hashem.
However, each nation continued to make its own gods and to set them up in the cult places which had been made by the people of Shomron; each nation [set them up] in the towns in which it lived.
The Bavel made Sukot Bnot, and the men of Kut made Nergal, and the men of Chamat made Ashima,
and the Avvites made Nivchaz and Tartak; and the Sepharvites burned their children [as offerings] to Adramelech and Anamelech, the gods of Sfarvayim.
They worshiped Hashem, but they also appointed from their own ranks priests of the shrines, who officiated for them in the cult places.
They worshiped Hashem, while serving their own gods according to the practices of the nations from which they had been deported.

To this day, they follow their former practices. They do not worship Hashem [properly]. They do not follow the laws and practices, the Teaching and Instruction that Hashem enjoined upon the descendants of Yaakov—who was given the name Yisrael—
with whom He made a covenant and whom He commanded: “You shall worship no other gods; you shall not bow down to them nor serve them nor sacrifice to them.

You must worship only Hashem your God, who brought you out of the land of Mitzrayim with great might and with an outstretched arm: to Him alone shall you bow down and to Him alone shall you sacrifice.
You shall observe faithfully, all your days, the laws and the practices; the Teaching and Instruction that IcHeb. “He.” wrote down for you; do not worship other gods.
Do not forget the covenant that I made with you; do not worship other gods.
Worship only Hashem your Elokim, and He will save you from the hands of all your enemies.”
But they did not obey; they continued their former practices.
Those nations worshiped Hashem, but they also served their idols. To this day their children and their children’s children do as their ancestors did.
In the third year of King Hoshea son of Elah of Yisrael, Chizkiyahu son of King Achaz of Yehudah became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yerushalayim twenty-nine years; his mother’s name was AviaDivrei Hayamim II 29.1 reads “Aviyah.” daughter of Zecharyah.
He did what was pleasing to Hashem, just as his father David had done.

He abolished the shrines and smashed the pillars and cut down the sacred post. He also broke into pieces the bronze serpent that Moshe had made, for until that time Bnei Yisrael had been offering sacrifices to it; it was called Nechushtan.
He trusted only in Hashem the Elokim of Yisrael; there was none like him among all the kings of Yehudah after him, nor among those before him.
He clung to Hashem; he did not turn away from following Him, but kept the commandments that Hashem had given to Moshe.
And Hashem was always with him; he was successful wherever he turned. He rebelled against the king of Ashur and would not serve him.
He overran Peleshet as far as Azah and its border areas, from watchtower to fortified town.
In the fourth year of King Chizkiyahu, which was the seventh year of King Hoshea son of Elah of Yisrael, King Shalmaneser of Ashur marched against Shomron and besieged it,

and hebSo some mss. and ancient versions; most mss. and editions read “they.” captured it at the end of three years. In the sixth year of Chizkiyahu, which was the ninth year of King Hoshea of Yisrael, Shomron was captured;
and the king of Ashur deported Bnei Yisrael to Ashur. He cLit. “led them to.”settled them in-c Chlach, along the Chavor [and] the River Gozan, and in the towns of Madai.
[This happened] because they did not obey Hashem their Elokim; they transgressed His covenant—all that Moshe the servant of Hashem had commanded. They did not obey and they did not fulfill it.
In the fourteenth year of King Chizkiyahu, King Sancheriv of Ashur marched against all the fortified towns of Yehudah and seized them.

King Chizkiyahu sent this message to the king of Ashur at Lachish: “I have done wrong; withdraw from me; and I shall bear whatever you impose on me.” So the king of Ashur imposed upon King Chizkiyahu of Yehudah a payment of three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
Chizkiyahu gave him all the silver that was on hand in the House of Hashem and in the treasuries of the palace.
At that time Chizkiyahu cut down the doors and the doorpostsdMeaning of Heb. uncertain. of the Temple of Hashem, which King Chizkiyahu had overlaid [with gold], and gave them to the king of Ashur.

But the king of Ashur sent eAshuri titles.the Tartan, the Rabsaris, and the Ravshake-e from Lachish with a large force to King Chizkiyahu in Yerushalayim. They marched up to Yerushalayim; and when they arrived, they took up a position near the conduit of the Upper Pool, by the road of the Fuller’s Field.
They summoned the king; and Elyakim son of Chilkiyahu, who was in charge of the palace, Shevna the scribe, and Yoach son of Asaf the recorder went out to them.
The Ravshake said to them, “You tell Chizkiyahu: Thus said the Great King, the King of Ashur: What makes you so confident?
You must think that mere talk is counsel and valor for war! Look, on whom are you relying, that you have rebelled against me?

You rely, of all things, on Mitzrayim, that splintered reed of a staff, which enters and punctures the palm of anyone who leans on it! That’s what Paroh king of Mitzrayim is like to all who rely on him.

And if you tell me that you are relying on Hashem your Elokim, He is the very one whose shrines and altars Chizkiyahu did away with, telling Yehudah and Yerushalayim, ‘You must worship only at this altar in Yerushalayim.’
Come now, make this wager with my master, the king of Ashur: I’ll give you two thousand horses if you can produce riders to mount them.
So how could you refuse anything even to the deputy of one of my master’s lesser servants, relying on Mitzrayim for chariots and horsemen?
And do you think I have marched against this land to destroy it without Hashem? Hashem Himself told me: Go up against that land and destroy it.”

Elyakim son of Chilkiyahu, Shevna, and Yoach replied to the Ravshake, “Please, speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it; do not speak to us in Yehudi in the hearing of the people on the wall.”

But the Ravshake answered them, “Was it to your master and to you that my master sent me to speak those words? It was precisely to the men who are sitting on the wall—who will have to eat their dung and drink their urine with you.”
And the Ravshake stood and called out in a loud voice in Yehudi: “Hear the words of the Great King, the King of Ashur.
Thus said the king: Don’t let Chizkiyahu deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you from myfSo several mss. and ancient versions; most mss. and editions read “his.” hands.
Don’t let Chizkiyahu make you rely on Hashem, saying: Hashem will surely save us: this city will not fall into the hands of the king of Ashur.

Don’t listen to Chizkiyahu. For thus said the king of Ashur: Make your peace with me and come out to me,gI.e., to my representative the Ravshake. so that you may all eat from your vines and your fig trees and drink water from your cisterns,

until I come and take you away to a land like your own, a land of grain [fields] and vineyards, of bread and wine, of olive oil and honey, so that you may live and not die. Don’t listen to Chizkiyahu, who misleads you by saying, ‘Hashem will save us.’
Did any of the gods of other nations save his land from the king of Ashur?
Where were the gods of Chamat and Arpad? Where were the gods of Sfarvayim, Hena, and Ivah? [And] did theyhI.e., the gods of Shomron. save Shomron from me?
Which among all the gods of [those] countries saved their countries from me, that Hashem should save Yerushalayim from me?”
But the people were silent and did not say a word in reply; for the king’s order was: “Do not answer him.”

And so Elyakim son of Chilkiyahu, who was in charge of the palace, Shevna the scribe, and Yoach son of Asaf the recorder came to Chizkiyahu with their clothes rent, and they reported to him what the Ravshake had said.
When King Chizkiyahu heard this, he rent his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the House of Hashem.
He also sent Elyakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shevna the scribe, and the senior priests, covered with sackcloth, to the prophet Yeshayahu son of Amotz.

They said to him, “Thus said Chizkiyahu: This day is a day of distress, of chastisement, and of disgrace. aI.e., the situation is desperate and we are at a loss.The babes have reached the birthstool, but the strength to give birth is lacking.-a

Perhaps Hashem your Elokim will take note of all the words of the Ravshake, whom his master the king of Ashur has sent to blaspheme the living Elokim, and will mete out judgment for the words that Hashem your Elokim has heard—if you will offer up prayer for the surviving remnant.”
When King Chizkiyahu’s ministers came to Yeshayahu,
Yeshayahu said to them, “Tell your master as follows: Thus said Hashem: Do not be frightened by the words of blasphemy against Me that you have heard from the minions of the king of Ashur.
I will deludebLit. “put a spirit in.” him; he will hear a rumor and return to his land, and I will make him fall by the sword in his land.”
The Ravshake, meanwhile, heard that [the king] had left Lachish; he turned back and found the king of Ashur attacking Livnah.
But [the king of Ashur] learned that King Tirhakah of Kush had come out to fight him; so he again sent messengers to Chizkiyahu, saying,
“Tell this to King Chizkiyahu of Yehudah: Do not let your Elokim, on whom you are relying, mislead you into thinking that Yerushalayim will not be delivered into the hands of the king of Ashur.
You yourself have heard what the kings of Ashur have done to all the lands, how they have annihilated them; and can you escape?
Were the nations that my predecessorscLit. “fathers.” destroyed—Gozan, Charan, Retzef, and the Beth-edenites in Tlasar—saved by their gods?
Where is the king of Chamat? And the king of Arpad? And the kings of Lair, Sfarvayim, Hena, and Ivah?”
Chizkiyahu took the letter from the messengers and read it. Chizkiyahu then went up to the House of Hashem and spread it out before Hashem.
And Chizkiyahu prayed to Hashem and said, “O Hashem of Hosts, Enthroned on the Keruvim! You alone are Elokim of all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
O Hashem, incline Your ear and hear; open Your eyes and see. Hear the words that Sancheriv has sent to blaspheme the living Elokim!
True, O Hashem, the kings of Ashur have annihilated the nations and their lands,
and have committed their gods to the flames and have destroyed them; for they are not gods, but man’s handiwork of wood and stone.
But now, O Hashem our Elokim, deliver us from his hands, and let all the kingdoms of the earth know that You alone, O Hashem, are Elokim.”
Then Yeshayahu son of Amotz sent this message to Chizkiyahu: “Thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael: I have heard the prayer you have offered to Me concerning King Sancheriv of Ashur.

This is the word that Hashem has spoken concerning him:

“Fair Maiden Tziyon despises you,
She mocks at you;
Fair Yerushalayim shakes
Her head at you.

Whom have you blasphemed and reviled?
Against whom made loud your voice
And haughtily raised your eyes?
Against the Holy One of Yisrael!

Through your envoys you have blasphemed my Lord.
Because you thought,
‘Thanks to my vast chariotry,
It is I who have climbed the highest mountains,
To the remotest parts of the Levanon,
And have cut down its loftiest cedars,
Its choicest cypresses,
And have reached its dYeshayahu 37.24 reads “highest peak.”remotest lodge,-d
eLit. “Its farmland forest”; exact meaning of Heb. uncertain.Its densest forest.-e

It is I who have drawnfOr “dug”; meaning of Heb. uncertain. and drunk the waters of strangers;
I have dried up with the soles of my feet
All the streams of Mitzrayim.’

Have you not heard? Of old
I planned that very thing,
I designed it long ago,
And now have fulfilled it.
And it has come to pass,
Laying waste fortified towns
In desolate heaps.

Their inhabitants are helpless,
Dismayed and shamed.
They were but grass of the field
And green herbage,
Grass of the roofs that is blasted
Before the gEmendation yields “east wind”; see note at Yeshayahu 37.27.standing grain.-g

I know your stayings
And your goings and comings,
And how you have raged against Me.

Because you have raged against Me,
And your tumult has reached My ears,
I will place My hook in your nose
And My bit between your jaws;
And I will make you go back by the road
By which you came.

“And this is the sign for you:hI.e., Chizkiyahu. This year you eat what grows of itself, and the next year what springs from that; and in the third year, sow and reap, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
And the survivors of the House of Yehudah that have escaped shall regenerate its stock below and produce boughs above.

For a remnant shall come forth from Yerushalayim,
Survivors from Mount Tziyon.
The zeal of Hashem of Hosts
Shall bring this to pass.

Assuredly, thus said Hashem concerning the king of Ashur:

He shall not enter this city:
He shall not shoot an arrow at it,
Or advance upon it with a shield,
Or pile up a siege mound against it.

He shall go back
By the way he came;
He shall not enter this city
—declares Hashem.

I will protect and save this city for My sake,
And for the sake of My servant David.”
That night an angel of Hashem went out and struck down one hundred and eighty-five thousand in the Ashuri camp, and the following morning they were all dead corpses.
So King Sancheriv of Ashur broke camp and retreated, and stayed in Nineveh.

While he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adramelech and Saretzer struck him down with the sword. They fled to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarchadon succeeded him as king.
In those days Chizkiyahu fell dangerously ill. The prophet Yeshayahu son of Amotz came and said to him, “Thus said Hashem: Set your affairs in order, for you are going to die; you will not get well.”
Thereupon Chizkiyahu turned his face to the wall and prayed to Hashem. He said,
“Please, O Hashem, remember how I have walked before You sincerely and wholeheartedly, and have done what is pleasing to You.” And Chizkiyahu wept profusely.
Before Yeshayahu had gone out of the middle court, the word of Hashem came to him:

“Go back and say to Chizkiyahu, the ruler of My people: Thus said Hashem, the Elokim of your father David: I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears. I am going to heal you; on the third day you shall go up to the House of Hashem.
And I will add fifteen years to your life. I will also rescue you and this city from the hands of the king of Ashur. I will protect this city for My sake and for the sake of My servant David.”—
Then Yeshayahu said, “Get a cake of figs.” And they got one, and they applied it to the rash, and he recovered.—
Chizkiyahu asked Yeshayahu, “What is the sign that Hashem will heal me and that I shall go up to the House of Hashem on the third day?”
Yeshayahu replied, “This is the sign for you from Hashem that Hashem will do the thing that He has promised: ShallaCf. Targum. the shadow advance ten steps or recede ten steps?”
Chizkiyahu said, “It is easy for the shadow to lengthen ten steps, but not for the shadow to recede ten steps.”

So the prophet Yeshayahu called to Hashem, and He made the shadow which had descended on the dialbHeb. “steps.” A model of a dial with steps has been discovered in Mitzrayim. of Achaz recede ten steps.

At that time, King Berodach-cSeveral mss. and the parallel Yeshayahu 39.1 read “Merodach.”baladan son of Baladan of Bavel sent [envoys with] a letter and a gift to Chizkiyahu, for he had heard about Chizkiyahu’s illness.

dYeshayahu 39.2 reads “Chizkiyahu was pleased by their coming.”Chizkiyahu heard about them-d and he showed them all his treasure-house—the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fragrant oil—and his armory, and everything that was to be found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his palace or in all his realm that Chizkiyahu did not show them.

Then the prophet Yeshayahu came to King Chizkiyahu. “What,” he demanded of him, “did those men say to you? Where have they come to you from?” “They have come,” Chizkiyahu replied, “from a far country, from Bavel.”
Next he asked, “What have they seen in your palace?” And Chizkiyahu replied, “They have seen everything that is in my palace. There was nothing in my storehouses that I did not show them.”
Then Yeshayahu said to Chizkiyahu, “Hear the word of Hashem:
A time is coming when everything in your palace which your ancestors have stored up to this day will be carried off to Bavel; nothing will remain behind, said Hashem.
And some of your sons, your own issue, whom you will have fathered, will be taken to serve as eunuchs in the palace of the king of Bavel.”
Chizkiyahu declared to Yeshayahu, “The word of Hashem that you have spoken is good.” For he thought, “It means that eLit. “there shall be safety and faithfulness in.”safety is assured for-e my time.”
The other events of Chizkiyahu’s reign, and all his exploits, and how he made the pool and the conduit and brought the water into the city, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yehudah.
Chizkiyahu slept with his fathers, and his son Menashe succeeded him as king.
Menashe was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Yerushalayim; his mother’s name was Hephzibah.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem, following the abhorrent practices of the nations that Hashem had dispossessed before Bnei Yisrael.

He rebuilt the shrines that his father Chizkiyahu had destroyed; he erected altars for Ba'al and made a sacred post, as King Achav of Yisrael had done. He bowed down to all the host of heaven and worshiped them,
and he built altars for them in the House of Hashem, of which Hashem had said, “I will establish My name in Yerushalayim.”
He built altars for all the hosts of heaven in the two courts of the House of Hashem.
He consigned his son to the fire; he practiced soothsaying and divination, and consulted ghosts and familiar spirits; he did much that was displeasing to Hashem, to vex Him.

The sculptured image of Asherah that he made he placed in the House concerning which Hashem had said to David and to his son Shlomo, “In this House and in Yerushalayim, which I chose out of all the tribes of Yisrael, I will establish My name forever.

And I will not again cause the feet of Yisrael to wander from the land that I gave to their fathers, if they will but faithfully observe all that I have commanded them—all the Teachings with which My servant Moshe charged them.”
But they did not obey, and Menashe led them astray to do greater evil than the nations that Hashem had destroyed before Bnei Yisrael.
Therefore Hashem spoke through His servants the prophets:
“Because King Menashe of Yehudah has done these abhorrent things—he has outdone in wickedness all that the Emori did before his time—and because he led Yehudah to sin with his fetishes,
assuredly, thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael: I am going to bring such a disaster on Yerushalayim and Yehudah that both ears of everyone who hears about it will tingle.

I will aI.e., I will bring the same fate upon it.apply to Yerushalayim the measuring line of Shomron and the weights of the House of Achav;-a I will wipe Yerushalayim clean as one wipes a dish and turns it upside down.
And I will cast off the remnant of My own people and deliver them into the hands of their enemies. They shall be plunder and prey to all their enemies
because they have done what is displeasing to Me and have been vexing Me from the day that their fathers came out of Mitzrayim to this day.”
Moreover, Menashe put so many innocent persons to death that he filled Yerushalayim [with blood] from end to end—besides the sin he committed in causing Yehudah to do what was displeasing to Hashem.
The other events of Menashe’s reign, and all his actions, and the sins he committed, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yehudah.
Menashe slept with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his palace, in the garden of Uza; and his son Amon succeeded him as king.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Yerushalayim; his mother’s name was Meshulemet daughter of Charutz of Yotvah.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem, as his father Menashe had done.
He walked in all the ways of his father, worshiping the fetishes which his father had worshiped and bowing down to them.
He forsook Hashem, the Elokim of his fathers, and did not follow the way of Hashem.
Amon’s courtiers conspired against him; and they killed the king in his palace.
But the people of the land put to death all who had conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land made his son Yoshiyahu king in his stead.
The other events of Amon’s reign [and] his actions are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yehudah.
He was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uza; and his son Yoshiyahu succeeded him as king.
Yoshiyahu was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Yerushalayim. His mother’s name was Yedidah daughter of Adayah of Botzkat.
He did what was pleasing to Hashem and he followed all the ways of his ancestor David; he did not deviate to the right or to the left.
In the eighteenth year of King Yoshiyahu, the king sent the scribe Shafan son of Atzalyahu son of Meshulam to the House of Hashem, saying,

“Go to the high priest Chilkiyahu and let him weighaMeaning of Heb. uncertain. Emendation yields “melt down,” cf. v. 9. the silver that has been deposited in the House of Hashem, which the guards of the threshold have collected from the people.

And let it be delivered to the overseers of the work who are in charge at the House of Hashem, that they in turn may pay it out to the workmen that are in the House of Hashem, for the repair of the House:
to the carpenters, the laborers, and the masons, and for the purchase of wood and quarried stones for repairing the House.
However, no check is to be kept on them for the silver that is delivered to them, for they deal honestly.”
Then the high priest Chilkiyahu said to the scribe Shafan, “I have found a scroll of the Teaching in the House of Hashem.” And Chilkiyahu gave the scroll to Shafan, who read it.

The scribe Shafan then went to the king and reported to the king: “Your servants have melted down the silver that was deposited in the House, and they have delivered it to the overseers of the work who are in charge at the House of Hashem.”
The scribe Shafan also told the king, “The high priest Chilkiyahu has given me a scroll”; and Shafan read it to the king.
When the king heard the words of the scroll of the Teaching, he rent his clothes.
And the king gave orders to the priest Chilkiyahu, and to Achikam son of Shafan, Achbor son of Michayah, the scribe Shafan, and Asayah the king’s minister:

“Go, inquire of Hashem on my behalf, and on behalf of the people, and on behalf of all Yehudah, concerning the words of this scroll that has been found. For great indeed must be the wrath of Hashem that has been kindled against us, because our fathers did not obey the words of this scroll to do all that has been prescribed for us.”

So the priest Chilkiyahu, and Achikam, Achbor, Shafan, and Asayah went to the prophetess Chuldah—the wife of Shalum son of Tikvah son of Charchas, the keeper of the wardrobe—who was living in Yerushalayim in the Mishne,bA quarter in Yerushalayim; cf. Tzefanyah 1.10. and they spoke to her.
She responded: “Thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael: Say to the man who sent you to me:
Thus said Hashem: I am going to bring disaster upon this place and its inhabitants, in accordance with all the words of the scroll which the king of Yehudah has read.
Because they have forsaken Me and have made offerings to other gods and vexed Me with all their deeds, My wrath is kindled against this place and it shall not be quenched.
But say this to the king of Yehudah, who sent you to inquire of Hashem: Thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael: As for the words which you have heard—

because your heart was softened and you humbled yourself before Hashem when you heard what I decreed against this place and its inhabitants—that it will become a desolation and a curse—and because you rent your clothes and wept before Me, I for My part have listened—declares Hashem.

Assuredly, I will gather you to your fathers and you will be laid in your tomb in peace. Your eyes shall not see all the disaster which I will bring upon this place.” So they brought back the reply to the king.
At the king’s summons, all the elders of Yehudah and Yerushalayim assembled before him.

The king went up to the House of Hashem, together with all the men of Yehudah and all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, and the priests and prophets—all the people, young and old. And he read to them the entire text of the covenant scroll which had been found in the House of Hashem.

The king stood aOr “on a platform,” cf. Targum.by the pillar-a and solemnized the covenant before Hashem: that they would follow Hashem and observe His commandments, His injunctions, and His laws with all their heart and soul; that they would fulfill all the terms of this covenant as inscribed upon the scroll. And all the people bCf. Targum.entered into-b the covenant.

Then the king ordered the high priest Chilkiyahu, the priests of the second rank, and the guards of the threshold to bring out of the Temple of Hashem all the objects made for Ba'al and AsherahcFor this goddess, cf. Melachim I 18.19; ordinarily asherah is rendered “sacred post,” e.g., Melachim II 17.16. and all the host of heaven. He burned them outside Yerushalayim in the fieldsdMeaning of Heb. uncertain. of Kidron, and he removed the ashes to Beit El.

He suppressed the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Yehudah had appointed eLit. “and he offered.”to make offerings-e at the shrines in the towns of Yehudah and in the environs of Yerushalayim, and those who made offerings to Ba'al, to the sun and moon and constellations—all the host of heaven.

He brought out the [image of] Asherah from the House of Hashem to the Kidron Valley outside Yerushalayim, and burned it in the Kidron Valley; he beat it to dust and scattered its dust over the burial ground of the common people.
He tore down the cubicles of the male prostitutes in the House of Hashem, at the place where the women wove coveringsdMeaning of Heb. uncertain. for Asherah.

He brought all the priests from the towns of Yehudah [to Yerushalayim] and defiled the shrines where the priests had been making offerings—from Geva to Beer Sheva. He also demolished the shrines of the gates, which were at the entrance of the gate of Yehoshua, the city prefect—dMeaning of Heb. uncertain.which were on a person’s left [as he entered] the city gate.-d

fThis verse may be understood in connection with vv. 21–23.The priests of the shrines, however, did not ascend the altar of Hashem in Yerushalayim, but they ate unleavened bread along with their kinsmen.-f
He also defiled Tofet, which is in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, so that no one might consign his son or daughter to the fire of Molech.

He did away with the horses that the kings of Yehudah had dedicated to the sun, gHeb. “from entering.”at the entrance-g of the House of Hashem, near the chamber of the eunuch Netan Melech, which was in the precincts.dMeaning of Heb. uncertain. He burned the chariots of the sun.

And the king tore down the altars made by the kings of Yehudah on the roof by the upper chamber of Achaz, and the altars made by Menashe in the two courts of the House of Hashem. He hHeb. “ran from there.” Emendation yields “smashed them there.”removed them quickly from there-h and scattered their rubble in the Kidron Valley.

The king also defiled the shrines facing Yerushalayim, to the south of the iHeb. har ha-mashḥith: a derogatory play on har ha-mishḥah (“Mount of Ointment”); Mishnah Middoth 2.4.Mount of the Destroyer,-i which King Shlomo of Yisrael had built for Ashtoret, the abomination of the Tzidonim, for Kmosh, the abomination of Moav, and for Milkom, the detestable thing of Bnei Amon.jCf. Melachim I 11.5, 7.
He shattered their pillars and cut down their sacred posts and covered their sites with human bones.

As for the altar in Beit El [and] the shrine made by Yerovam son of Nevat who caused Yisrael to sin—that altar, too, and the shrine as well, he tore down. He burned down the shrine and beat it to dust, and he burned the sacred post.

Yoshiyahu turned and saw the graves that were there on the hill; and he had the bones taken out of the graves and burned on the altar. Thus he defiled it, in fulfillment of the word of Hashem foretold by the man of Elokim who foretold these happenings.

He asked, “What is the marker I see there?” And the men of the town replied, “That is the grave of the man of God who came from Yehudah and foretold these things that you have done to the altar of Beit El.”kCf. Melachim I 13.2–3.

“Let him be,” he said, “let no one disturb his bones.” So they left his bones undisturbed together with the bones of the prophetlSee Melachim I 13.31–32 and note m below. who came from Shomron.mThe prophet lived in Beit El, which, in Yoshiyahu’s time, was part of the Ashuri province of Shomron.
Yoshiyahu also abolished all the cult places in the towns of Shomron, which the kings of Yisrael had built, vexing [Hashem]. He dealt with them just as he had done to Beit El:
He slew on the altars all the priests of the shrines who were there, and he burned human bones on them. Then he returned to Yerushalayim.
The king commanded all the people, “Offer the passover sacrifice to Hashem your Elokim as prescribed in this scroll of the covenant.”
Now the passover sacrifice had not been offered in that manner in the days of the chieftains who ruled Yisrael, or during the days of the kings of Yisrael and the kings of Yehudah.
Only in the eighteenth year of King Yoshiyahu was such a passover sacrifice offered in that manner to Hashem in Yerushalayim.

Yoshiyahu also did away with nLit. “the ghosts and the familiar spirits.”the necromancers and the mediums,-n the idols and the fetishes—all the detestable things that were to be seen in the land of Yehudah and Yerushalayim. Thus he fulfilled the terms of the Teaching recorded in the scroll that the priest Chilkiyahu had found in the House of Hashem.
There was no king like him before who turned back to Hashem with all his heart and soul and might, in full accord with the Teaching of Moshe; nor did any like him arise after him.
However, Hashem did not turn away from His awesome wrath which had blazed up against Yehudah because of all the things Menashe did to vex Him.
Hashem said, “I will also banish Yehudah from My presence as I banished Yisrael; and I will reject the city of Yerushalayim which I chose and the House where I said My name would abide.”
The other events of Yoshiyahu’s reign, and all his actions, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yehudah.

In his days, Paroh Necho, king of Mitzrayim, marched against the king of AshuroI.e., the Kasdi Empire; cf. Yeshayahu 52.4 and note. to the River Perat; King Yoshiyahu marched toward him, but when he confronted him at Megiddo, [Paroh Necho] slew him.

His servants conveyed his body in a chariot from Megiddo to Yerushalayim, and they buried him in his tomb. Then the people of the land took Yehoachaz; they anointed him and made him king in place of his father.
Yehoachaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Yerushalayim; his mother’s name was Chamutal daughter of Yirmiyahu of Livnah.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem, just as his fathers had done.
Paroh Necho imprisoned him in Rivlah in the region of Chamat, to keep him from reigning in Yerushalayim. And he imposed on the land an indemnity of one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

Then Paroh Necho appointed Elyakim son of Yoshiyahu king in place of his father Yoshiyahu, changing his name to Yehoyakim. He took Yehoachaz and pSo Divrei Hayamim II 36.4; Heb. here “he came.”brought him-p to Mitzrayim, where he died.

Yehoyakim gave Paroh the silver and the gold, and he made an assessment on the land to pay the money demanded by Paroh. He exacted from the people of the land the silver and gold to be paid Paroh Necho, according to each man’s assessment.
Yehoyakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim; his mother’s name was Zvudah daughter of Pedayah of Rumah.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem, just as his ancestors had done.
In his days, King Nevuchadnetzar of Bavel came up, and Yehoyakim became his vassal for three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.

Hashem let loose against him the raiding bands of the Kasdim, Aram, Moavim, and Bnei Amon; He let them loose against Yehudah to destroy it, in accordance with the word that Hashem had spoken through His servants the prophets.
All this befell Yehudah at the command of Hashem, who banished [them] from His presence because of all the sins that Menashe had committed,
and also because of the blood of the innocent that he shed. For he filled Yerushalayim with the blood of the innocent, and Hashem would not forgive.
The other events of Yehoyakim’s reign, and all of his actions, are recorded in the Annals of the Kings of Yehudah.
Yehoyakim slept with his fathers, and his son Yehoyachin succeeded him as king.

The king of Mitzrayim did not venture out of his country again, for the king of Bavel had seized all the land that had belonged to the king of Mitzrayim, from the Wadi of Mitzrayim to the River Perat.
Yehoyachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Yerushalayim; his mother’s name was Nechushta daughter of Elnatan of Yerushalayim.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem, just as his father had done.
At that time, the troopsaHeb. “servants.” of King Nevuchadnetzar of Bavel marched against Yerushalayim, and the city came under siege.
King Nevuchadnetzar of Bavel advanced against the city while his troops were besieging it.

Thereupon King Yehoyachin of Yehudah, along with his mother, and his courtiers, commanders, and officers, surrendered to the king of Bavel. The king of Bavel took him captive in the eighth year of his reign.

He carried off bHeb. “from there.”from Yerushalayim-b all the treasures of the House of Hashem and the treasures of the royal palace; he stripped off all the golden decorations in the Temple of Hashem—which King Shlomo of Yisrael had made—as Hashem had warned.
He exiled all of Yerushalayim: all the commanders and all the warriors—ten thousand exiles—as well as all the craftsmen and smiths; only the poorest people in the land were left.
He deported Yehoyachin to Bavel; and the king’s mother and wives and officers and the notables of the land were brought as exiles from Yerushalayim to Bavel.
All the able men, to the number of seven thousand—all of them warriors, trained for battle—and a thousand craftsmen and smiths were brought to Bavel as exiles by the king of Bavel.
And the king of Bavel appointed Matanyah, Yehoyachin’scHeb. “his.” uncle, king in his place, changing his name to Tzidkiyahu.

dFor the rest of this book cf. Yirmiyahu 39 and 52.Tzidkiyahu was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim; his mother’s name was Chamutal daughter of Yirmiyahu of Livnah.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem, just as Yehoyakim had done.

Indeed, Yerushalayim and Yehudah eMeaning of Heb. uncertain.were a cause of anger for Hashem, so that-e He cast them out of His presence.
Tzidkiyahu rebelled against the king of Bavel.

And in the ninth year of hisaI.e., Tzidkiyahu’s. reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nevuchadnetzar moved against Yerushalayim with his whole army. He besieged it; and they built towers against it all around.
The city continued in a state of siege until the eleventh year of King Tzidkiyahu.
By the ninth day [of the fourth month]bCf. Yirmiyahu 52.6. the famine had become acute in the city; there was no food left for the common people.

Then [the wall of] the city was breached. All the soldiers [left the city] by night through the gate between the double walls, which is near the king’s garden—the Kasdim were all around the city; and [the king] set out for the Arabah.cHoping to escape across the Yarden.
But the Kasdi troops pursued the king, and they overtook him in the steppes of Yericho as his entire force left him and scattered.
They captured the king and brought him before the king of Bavel at Rivlah; and they put him on trial.
They slaughtered Tzidkiyahu’s sons before his eyes; then Tzidkiyahu’s eyes were put out. He was chained in bronze fetters and he was brought to Bavel.
On the seventh day of the fifth month—that was the nineteenth year of King Nevuchadnetzar of Bavel—Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, an officer of the king of Bavel, came to Yerushalayim.
He burned the House of Hashem, the king’s palace, and all the houses of Yerushalayim; he burned down dMeaning of Heb. uncertain.the house of every notable person.-d
The entire Kasdi force that was with the chief of the guard tore down the walls of Yerushalayim on every side.

The remnant of the people that was left in the city, the defectors who had gone over to the king of Bavel—and the remnant of the population—were taken into exile by Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards.
But some of the poorest in the land were left by the chief of the guards, to be vinedressers and field hands.
The Kasdim broke up the bronze columns of the House of Hashem, the stands, and the bronze tank that was in the House of Hashem; and they carried the bronze away to Bavel.
They also took all the pails, scrapers, snuffers, ladles, and all the other bronze vessels used in the service.
The chief of the guards took whatever was of gold and whatever was of silver: firepans and sprinkling bowls.
The two columns, the one tank, and the stands that Shlomo provided for the House of Hashem—all these objects contained bronze beyond weighing.

The one column was eighteen cubits high. It had a bronze capital above it; the height of the capital was three cubits, and there was a meshwork [decorated] with pomegranates about the capital, all made of bronze. And the like was true of the other column with its meshwork.
The chief of the guards also took Srayah, the chief priest, Tzefanyah, the deputy priest, and the three guardians of the threshold.

And from the city he took a eunuch who was in command of the soldiers; five royal privy councillors who were present in the city; the scribe of the army commander, who was in charge of mustering the people of the land; and sixty of the common people who were inside the city.
Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, took them and brought them to the king of Bavel at Rivlah.

The king of Bavel had them struck down and put to death at Rivlah, in the region of Chamat.
Thus Yehudah was exiled from its land.
King Nevuchadnetzar of Bavel put Gedalyahu son of Achikam son of Shafan in charge of the people whom he left in the land of Yehudah.

When the officers of the troops and their men heard that the king of Bavel had put Gedalyahu in charge, they came to Gedalyahu at Mitzpah with Yishmael son of Netanyah, Yochanan son of Kareach, Srayah son of Tanchumet the Netofati, and Ya'azanyahu son of the Maachite, together with their men.

Gedalyahu reassuredeLit. “took an oath to them.” them and their men, saying, “Do not be afraid fYirmiyahu 40.9 reads “to serve the Kasdim.”of the servants of the Kasdim.-f Stay in the land and serve the king of Bavel, and it will go well with you.”

In the seventh month, Yishmael son of Netanyah son of Elishama, who was of royal descent, came with ten men, and they struck down Gedalyahu and he died; [they also killed] the Yehudim and the Kasdim who were present with him at Mitzpah.
And all the people, young and old, and the officers of the troops set out and went to Mitzrayim because they were afraid of the Kasdim.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of King Yehoyachin of Yehudah, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, King Evil Merodach of Bavel, in the year he became king, gLit. “raised the head of.”took note of-g King Yehoyachin of Yehudah and released him from prison.
He spoke kindly to him, and gave him a throne above those of other kings who were with him in Bavel.
His prison garments were removed, and [Yehoyachin] received regular rations by his favor for the rest of his life.
A regular allotment of food was given him at the instance of the king—an allotment for each day—all the days of his life.
